result:
In upstream mode, the `CONNECT` target and `Host` header now bracket IPv6 literals, so they read `[2001:db8::1]:443`. I haven't run any tests, per your instructions, so neither the new test nor the existing ones have been run.

**Fix** (`mitmproxy/proxy/layers/http/_upstream_proxy.py`): `start_handshake` now checks whether the target host is an IPv6 address using `ipaddress.IPv6Address`. If it is, it wraps the host in `[...]`. Otherwise it IDNA-encodes the host as before, so hostnames and IPv4 addresses are unchanged. The single `authority` value feeds both the request target and the `Host` header, so this one change fixes both.

**Test** (`test/mitmproxy/proxy/layers/http/test_http.py`): I added `test_upstream_proxy_ipv6`. It drives `HTTPMode.upstream` with a `CONNECT [2001:db8::1]:443` from the client. It then asserts the request sent to the upstream proxy is `CONNECT [2001:db8::1]:443` with `Host: [2001:db8::1]:443`. I modeled it on the https branch of `test_upstream_proxy`. I expect it to fail on the old code, but I haven't confirmed that.
